image_description: A grand, ornate Baroque-style pipe organ installed in a church gallery. The instrument features a symmetrical facade with multiple towers of vertical metal pipes of varying heights, creating a stepped silhouette around a central arched window. The case is elaborately decorated with gold leaf, green and red accents, and sculptural elements including angels and cherubs. The organ sits on a white balcony with decorative moldings.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows multiple distinct groups (towers) of vertical pipes arranged in a highly symmetrical pattern relative to the central axis.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pipe heights range from very short compact pipes to dramatically towering pipes creating a dramatic stepped silhouette.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is a clear visual gradient in pipe height, with tall outer towers and shorter inner sections, creating the characteristic stepped profile of a pipe organ facade.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The console (keyboards and pedals) is typically located at the base of the organ or on the gallery floor, which is below the frame of this image. It is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Stop knobs are part of the console, which is not visible in this elevated shot of the facade.
